THE HEADLINES:-

 

  1. Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan begins landfall along North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts, close to Gopalpur.

     

  2. Prime Minister Narendra Modi calls for greater Jan Bhagidari in early identification of disabilities and overcoming social stigma.

     

  3. Prime Minister to inaugurate first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi this evening.

     

  4. 57th International Film Festival of India to begin today in Goa with grand opening ceremony.

     

  5. And, US, Chinese and Russian Presidents outline plans to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products to ease energy crisis.

Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan started making landfall along the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts, close to Gopalpur in Ganjam district. This was disclosed by India Meteorological Department (IMD) DG Mritunjay Mahapatra, a shortwhile ago. 

                                         

       

 

 

 

 

Bhubaneswar Met Office Director Manorama Mohanty said that landfall is expected to be completed between 10 am and 11 am. She said wind speeds are likely to reach 70 to 80 kilometres per hour, with gusts up to 90 kilometres per hour.

       

Meanwhile, heavy rainfall has started in several places and is likely to continue across the state for the next two days under the influence of the cyclone. In view of the cyclone and the prevailing adverse weather conditions, schools and Anganwadi centres have been closed in 15 districts of the state to ensure the safety of students and children. As a precautionary measure, the administration has evacuated and shifted over 3 lakh people to safer places.

       

 

IMD has issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts of Andhra. Our correspondent has filed this report on latest weather condition in Andhra Pradesh:

 

 

 

 

 

 

Heavy rainfall has been recorded in Srikakulam district, with 16 centimetres at Ichchapuram, 10 centimetres each at Kanchili and Kaviti, and 9.9 centimetres at Palasa. Light to moderate rain is likely over Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Godavari districts today. A flash-flood risk persists in some Srikakulam watersheds. Authorities are monitoring reservoirs, rivers and unsafe areas. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. People in low-lying and coastal areas have been urged to remain alert and follow official advisories. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.

       

In Jharkhand, Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega, Ramgarh, Ranchi, Khunti, Bokaro, Dhanbad, Saraikela-Kharsawan and West and East Singhbhum districts are expected to experience heavy rainfall today.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for greater Jan Bhagidari or community participation, in the early identification of disabilities and overcoming social stigma. Addressing the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment in New Delhi, Mr. Modi said, the community participation can play a significant role in creating awareness among parents about developmental disabilities and the importance of early identification. He emphasised that the spirit of competitive and cooperative federalism should guide implementation, with states learning from one another’s experiences and innovations. Mr Modi also advised that states could organise start-up competitions to encourage young innovators to develop affordable aids and assistive devices.

       

 

Highlighting the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan – Drug-Free India Campaign, The Prime Minister stressed that efforts to address substance abuse must go beyond routine and symbolic activities. He suggested involving schools through essay-writing, debates, oratory competitions, and other activities to generate awareness among young people and encourage wider societal participation.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi today. Mr Modi will also address the gathering on the occasion. More from our Correspondent:

       

The three day Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of the region, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation. The Forum will feature exhibitions showcasing India’s archaeological, artistic and literary heritage titled ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence. It will offer an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence. In the forum four thematic sessions will be held on Saturday and Sunday, bringing together scholars, academics, subject experts and cultural representatives. Discussions will cover cultural expressions such as music and performing arts, textiles, cuisine and traditional games. Shivang Mishra Akashvani News, Delhi.

<><><> 

       

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that in a “major milestone” in the fight against terrorism, Kashmir is free from India-born terrorists after 35 years. Addressing an anti-terror conference organised by NIA in New Delhi, Mr Shah said, with the elimination of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Lateef Bhat, the entire Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists. Bhat was neutralised by security forces on Wednesday in an encounter in South Kashmir’s Kulgam district. Carrying a reward of 15 lakh rupees, Bhat was wanted in connection with a November 11 attack on a CRPF post that left three paramilitary personnel injured.

       

Stressing the need to strengthen proactive action in the country’s counter-terrorism policy, Home Minister said that the entire terrorist network must be investigated and its capabilities dismantled in a coordinated manner. Mr Shah credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ‘zero-tolerance’ policy towards terrorism for yielding decisive results on the ground. He said, to eliminate the three menaces of terrorism, organised crime, and drugs, it is essential to bring the culprits and masterminds who have taken shelter abroad before Indian courts.

       

Mr Shah highlighted the government’s crackdown on transnational networks, stating that 303 fugitives have been brought back to India from 36 countries since 2019 through efforts by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Union Home Ministry, and intelligence agencies.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

 

The 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026 will begin today with a grand opening ceremony. Chief Minister Pramod Sawant and festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker will inaugurate the nine day cinematic extravaganza. The theme for this year’s IFFI is ‘Stories Without Borders’. More from our correspondent:

       

 

 

 

 

The International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026 kickstarts today with a grand opening ceremony planned in the evening. Goa is decked up with vibrant lights and decorations, in line with the theme of the festival, ‘Stories Without Borders’.

       

 

 

 

 

Featuring over 150 international films from 86 countries, IFFI 2026 promises a diverse cinematic experience, showcasing compelling narratives, emerging talent and acclaimed filmmakers. The festival will also provide a platform for meaningful conversations, masterclasses, industry interactions and discussions on the evolving landscape of world cinema.

       

 

 

 

 

Among the major highlights are the opening film, Fatherland, by Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski, and the closing film, We Are All Strangers, by Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen. With special sections on animation and films about filmmaking, alongside masterclasses, workshops, competitions and the WAVES Film Bazaar, IFFI 2026 aims to strengthen India’s engagement with the global film industry while celebrating the diversity and transformative power of cinema. IFFI 2026 promises to be not just a celebration of films but also a meeting ground for cultures, creative ideas and stories that transcend geographical and linguistic boundaries. With Alex and Vishnu, this is Saira Mujtaba, Panaji, Goa.

<><><> 

       

 

Government has approved the establishment of a Medical College at Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh’s Sarangpur campus. In a social media post, Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda said, this project will be developed at an investment of 456 crore rupees and will have an annual intake of 125 MBBS students. Spread across nearly 51 acres, the college will feature modern laboratories, advanced simulation facilities, clinical training and research infrastructure, nurturing the next generation of skilled medical professionals. Mr Nadda  added that  the approval marks another significant step towards fulfilling Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of adding 75 thousand medical seats in the country over the next five years. He said, the initiative will strengthen medical education and help develop a skilled healthcare workforce in the country.

<><><> 

       

Election Commission of India (ECI) has reviewed preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in Agra. The meeting, which covered 21 districts across five divisions, was chaired by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg, alongside Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa and other senior Commission officials. Administrative and police officials from the Agra, Bareilly, Jhansi, Kanpur, and Chitrakoot divisions also participated.

       

The review focused on preparing error-free electoral rolls, polling station arrangements, the availability and management of EVMs and VVPATs, training of election personnel, law and order, security arrangements, and monitoring of election expenditure.

       

Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa stated that webcasting will be arranged at all polling stations during the 2027 Assembly elections. GPS-enabled vehicles will be used for the secure transportation of EVMs. Nine Flying Squads and nine Static Surveillance Teams will be deployed in every Assembly constituency to monitor illegal cash, liquor, arms, narcotics, and other inducements. More than 20 central and state enforcement agencies will also be active during the election process.

Presidents of the US, China and Russia concluded their unprecedented trilateral meeting yesterday by issuing a Declaration Towards Peace, calling for UN reforms and outlining plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products to ease the energy crisis. The three Presidents Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin – in their four-point declaration also agreed to hold dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. They also agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met for the three-way summit on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen. Trump had expressed his intention to discuss nuclear arms reductions and other major international issues at the three-way summit.

<><><> 

       

India and Japan have unequivocally and strongly condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its form and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and called for action against all United Nations-listed terrorist groups and entities. The Joint Statement issued after Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar co-chaired the fourth India-Japan 2+2 Meeting in Tokyo called for concerted actions against all UN-listed terrorist groups and entities, including Al Qaeda, ISIS/Daesh, Lashkar-e-Tayyiba, Jaish-e-Mohammad and their proxies. 

<><><>

       

In Men’s Cricket, India were 16 for Nil in their first innings on second day of the first test against New Zealand at Wellington at tea. Earlier, the host posted a total of 368 runs in its first innings, with  Henry Nicholls anchors the innings an unbeaten 175 in 335 balls while, Glenn Phillips, contributed 118 runs in 216 balls. 

 

AND NOW, FOR A LOOK AT TODAY’S NEWSPAPERS,

 

 

 

 

 

 

  • “Tax cuts given, where are pay hikes, jobs? PM asks India Inc” headlines The Asian Age. Modi asks industry to use trade deals and expand globally.

  • Shenzhen peace declaration Trump, Xi, Putin agree on boosting oil supplies, reducing nuclear risks writes The Indian Express.

  • “Landmark EPFO plan allows monthly payouts to retirees” headlines The Tribune.

     

  • COP31: Future of fossil fuels exposes sharp divides among countries, yet again writes The Indian Express.

     

 

  • And finally, Purana Qila turns into heritage treasure trove. A live dig showcasing a Mauryan-era hearth, an 18th-century Mahabharata scroll and contemporary artist Subodh Gupta’s open-air monumental installation cast in stainless steel are some of the displays that PM Modi will view during SCO meet today leads The Hindustan Times.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi this morning. He will also address the gathering on this occasion. More from our correspondent:

“The convention, themed “Bharat 2047”, will bring together over two thousand 500 delegates, including industry leaders, CEOs, ambassadors, diplomats and policymakers. The year 2026-27 marks FICCI’s centenary year, as the organisation completes 100 years of its establishment in April next year. Established in 1927, FICCI was founded at a time when Indian enterprises had limited representation in economic policymaking. Since Independence, FICCI has been associated with India’s economic transformation and its growing integration with the global economy. Today, FICCI represents over 2.5 lakh companies across the public, private and multinational sectors, directly and through more than 300 affiliated regional and state-level industry associations. It has partnership agreements with 250 national business associations in over 100 countries. ANUPAM MISHRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has welcomed the growing momentum in India-UK bilateral relations, guided by India-UK Vision 2035 and strengthened by the entry into force of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) in July this year. Prime Minister Modi said this during his meeting with the Prince and Princess of Wales in New Delhi yesterday. Prime Minister Modi commended the work of the Earthshot Prize in encouraging innovative solutions to pressing environmental challenges. He appreciated its recognition of Indian innovators and their contributions to addressing global environmental challenges, including at the Earthshot Prize Awards held in Mumbai yesterday. The meeting also provided an opportunity to exchange views on further strengthening the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including cooperation in defense, health, education, fin-tech and people-to-people ties. Mr Modi also conveyed his warm regards to King Charles III and to Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment New Delhi this evening. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. It is the third in the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Prime Minister to strengthen cooperative federalism, foster collective ownership of national priorities and accelerate outcomes through closer Centre-State collaboration. The Summit will deliberate on four key thematic areas, Reimagining Prevention and Drug demand Reduction Strategy for a Nasha Mukt Bharat, One Nation One Scholarship portal- Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students, Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden and Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat.

External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will co chair the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue, also known as the 2+2 Dialogue with their Japanese counterparts, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizum in Tokyo today.

Earlier yesterday, addressing the inaugural Raisina Tokyo 2026 event, Dr. Jaishankar called for deeper India-Japan cooperation in key sectors, including semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and defence.

The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, will open to the general public at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from today. Organised annually by India Trade Promotion Organisation, it is one of India’s leading multi-product trade exhibitions. The theme this year is Vikas aur Virasat. A report:

“The 45th India International Trade Fair will open from 10 AM to 7:30 PM, while entry for the general public will be allowed until 5:30 PM. Tickets can be booked online through the official website, booking. Indiatradefair.com, and the IITF 2026 mobile application. Tickets are also available offline at 55 Delhi Metro stations. While season tickets are available for General Days. Senior citizens and persons with disabilities will be allowed free entry on General Days on production of a valid government-issued identity card. General visitors can enter the fair through Gate Numbers 3 and 4 on Bhairon Road and Gate Numbers 6 and 10 on Mathura Road. The trade fair will conclude on the 27th of this month. With Anupam and Anurag, Rishu Jaiswal, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the west central Bay of Bengal moved northwards and lay centered over the same region. It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh) and Puri (Odisha) tomorrow noon as a severe cyclonic storm. It will have the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kilometres per hour gusting to 110 kilometres per hour. The Met Department has advised fishermen not to venture into Southwest, Westcentral and Northwest Bay of Bengal till tomorrow.

The Weather Agency has issued a red colour warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha till tomorrow. According to IMD, places over Gangetic West Bengal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura will experience heavy rainfall during the same period.

<><><> 

The India Meteorological Centre says severe cyclonic storm Akvan is continuing over the west central Bay of Bengal and has moved with the speed of 5 kilometers per hour during last 6 hours. The storm is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by tomorrow afternoon. More from our correspondent:

“Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan is likely to bring moderate to heavy rain at some parts of Srikakulam district today. Moderate rain is also likely at some places in Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Polavaram, Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli districts. Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu has urged people in North Andhra Pradesh to remain alert and take precautionary measures. Farmers in Srikakulam have been asked to cover harvested paddy with tarpaulins and move it to safer places, if needed. The Andhra Pradesh government has put the administration on high alert. NDRF teams, SDRF teams and local fire service teams have been kept ready for emergency operations. Precautionary measures are being taken to prevent damage to power infrastructure due to strong winds along the coastal belt. People in cyclone-prone areas have been advised to remain alert and follow the instructions issued by the authorities. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

<><><> 

In view of the Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan, which is moving northwards over the west-central Bay of Bengal, posing a threat to the south Odisha coast the state government has intensified its disaster preparedness, deploying rescue teams and initiating evacuation measures in vulnerable districts. A Report:

“The India Meteorological Department says Cyclone Akvan is likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon tomorrow, with wind speeds of 90 to 100 kilometres per hour, gusting to 110 kilometres per hour. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected across Odisha, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over south Odisha. A storm surge of up to one metre may inundate low-lying areas of Ganjam and Puri. The State Government has deployed 60 ODRAF and 14 NDRF teams. Collectors of Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri have been directed to evacuate people from landslide-prone areas and open relief centres. Arrangements are also being made to ensure essential services and minimise damage. Prakash Dash for Akashvani  News, Bhubaneswar.”

The 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India is set to begin from tomorrow in Goa with a grand opening ceremony, inaugurated by Chief Minister Pramod Sawant. Over 150 International Films from 86 Countries will be bringing the World to Goa under the theme ‘Stories without Borders’, highlighting Cinema’s Power to Connect Cultures Across Borders. Acclaimed filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker is the festival director. This year’s special focus is on BRICS Cinema. Spain is the Country of Honour while Russia is the Partner Country. More from our correspondent:

“Goa is ready to roll out the red carpet for IFFI 2026 with many firsts happening this year. Fatherland’ is to Serve as the Opening Film of the 57th IFFI, ‘I Matter’ to Feature as Mid-Fest film, and ‘We Are All Strangers’ will Close the 57th edition of IFFI 2026. A dedicated segment will feature international animation films while for the very first time in the history of IFFI, a segment called ‘Films on Films’ has been curated mindfully on the suggestion of renowned filmmakers. India’s digital entertainment industry will also take centre stage as five distinctive web series will be nominated for the web series award in the OTT awards category. Ten Indian and international fiction feature films will compete for the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal. The award recognizes films that reflect Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals of non-violence, tolerance, intercultural understanding and a culture of peace. The nine day cinematic extravaganza will see films competing for the coveted Golden Peacock for Best film. Goa is ready, are you? With Alex and Vishnu, This Is Saira Mujtaba, Panaji, Goa.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has paid tributes to Rani Lakshmibai on her birth anniversary today. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that Rani Lakshmibai never compromised on her duty or self-respect, even in the most challenging circumstances. Mr Modi said that the story of her indomitable courage and extraordinary valor in the fight against foreign rule will continue to inspire every generation of this country to sacrifice everything for the motherland.

The Women’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 hockey tournament will begin in Bhopal today. The tournament will continue till 28th of this month. Apart from India, teams from China, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and Thailand will participate in the tournament. India has won this title three times in 2016, 2023 and 2024. India will begin its campaign against Malaysia at 7 PM today.

All six teams will play against each other in the league stage. Each team will play five matches, and the top four teams in the points table will qualify for the semi-finals.

In Men’s Cricket, the first test of the two match series between India and the hosts New Zealand is underway in Wellington. Put in to bat first, New Zealand lost early wickets. The hosts were 140 for 5 at tea, in their first innings.

The series marks the final leg of India’s tour of New Zealand, with valuable ICC World Test Championship points on the line. Steered by Shubman Gill, the 16-member squad features KL Rahul as vice-captain, alongside key players like Rishabh Pant, Jasprit Bumrah, and Ravindra Jadeja.

The Quad leaders have announced a series of initiatives to strengthen maritime security, artificial intelligence cooperation, cybersecurity and critical infrastructure connectivity across the Indo-Pacific at Manila Summit in Philippines. The summit brought together Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. In a joint press release, the four leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open, safe and prosperous Indo-Pacific, describing the Quad as a “partnership of action” dedicated to peace, stability and prosperity. The four countries also announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, scheduled to be held in early 2027.

<><><> 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi returned to New Delhi after successfully concluding his two-day visit to Manila, the Philippines. During the visit, Mr Modi participated in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, the 21st East Asia Summit and the Quad Leaders’ Meeting. The Prime Minister also visited the historic Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila and took part in the ceremony marking the commencement of its redevelopment.

At the Quad Summit, Mr Modi said for India, the Quad is a “constructive and trusted” partnership that strives to deliver trusted solutions across the Indo-Pacific, spanning maritime security, supply chains, new technologies, and disaster response.

<><><> 

The 49th ASEAN Summit 2026 in Manila concluded with a series of important outcomes aimed at strengthening India’s engagement with Southeast Asia and the wider Indo-Pacific region. A report:

“The outcomes from the ASEAN summit reflected India’s growing regional engagement and reinforced ASEAN’s central role in India’s Act East Policy and its vision of a free, open, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

At the ASEAN-India Summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed series of initiatives covering maritime security, cyber forensics, space, nuclear energy, critical minerals, youth exchanges and education. PM also announced free e-visas for ASEAN tourists and enhanced scholarships at Nalanda University.

Likewise at the East Asia Summit, the PM proposed initiatives on seafarers’ safety, cybercrime cooperation, maritime heritage and academic exchanges. Three important regional documents were adopted on disaster management, online scams and regional stability.

On the bilateral front, PM Modi held meetings with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and the Prime Ministers of Singapore and Thailand to expand cooperation in key sectors. Ishfaq Shah, Manila Philippines.”

Uttar Pradesh’s draft electoral roll for the 2027 Assembly elections has been published. It comprises 13.58 crore voters after a net addition of 18.84 lakh electorates during the Special Summary Revision. UP Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said, the draft roll updates the previous final list released on April 10, 2026, after the Special Intensive Revision. More from our correspondent;

“Out of a total of 13.58 voters, Men account for 7.38 crore, while Women account for 6.20 crore, reflecting an addition of nearly 11 lakh female electors since the April 2026 roll. The roll includes 4,042 third-gender electors. Citizens in the 18-19 age group represent 11.83 lakh of the total voters. The revision is being conducted with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligible citizens turning 18. Eligible residents can file their claims and objections from November 17 to December 16, 2026. Citizens can use Form 6 for new voter inclusion, Form 7 for deletion of names, and Form 8 for correcting existing entries. Election officials will resolve all submitted claims and objections by December 28, 2026. The final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027. Voters can inspect the roll at all 1,73,730 polling booths across the state’s 403 Assembly constituencies, or check their status online via the CEO Uttar Pradesh Portal. SUSHIL TIWARI, AKASHVANI NEWS , LUCKNOW.”

Northern Railway has successfully facilitated the travel of nearly 1.82 crore passengers during the Puja and festive season this year. It registered an increase of around 10 lakh passengers compared to the corresponding period last year. Through strategic capacity enhancement, an expanded fleet of special trains, coach augmentations, and continuous demand monitoring, the zone significantly outperformed its previous year’s operational benchmarks. A report:

“According to the Northern Railway, seven thousand 85 special train trips were operated during the festive season of Diwali and Chhath Puja, compared to four thousand 666 trips last year. This means around 54 additional special train trips were operated every day to manage the festive rush. Daily passenger handling also increased from approximately 3 lakh 91 thousand to 4 lakh 14 thousand, accommodating nearly 22 thousand 700 additional passengers every day. Of the total passengers carried, around 1 crore 66 lakh travelled through regular train services, while 12 lakh 83 thousand were accommodated through special Trains on Demand services. This is Dilnashi Arzoo, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

<><><> 

Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw  reviewed  the measures  to ensure passenger convenience and safety during the return journeys following the Chhath festival. Mr Vaishnaw, monitored live CCTV feeds from various railway stations to assess crowd levels and identify locations experiencing high passenger pressure. He directed officials to take  measures to ensure smooth operation of trains and the safety of passengers in view of the heavy crowd. He also reviewed the holding areas established for passengers at major stations, including Patna, Danapur, Rajendra Nagar Terminal, Saharsa, Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga, and Jaynagar.

Cyclonic Storm Akvan formed over Bay of Bengal is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that cyclone Akvan will intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by this morning and further intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow evening.
